description: THE MONEY ONE ACTIVITY CONSUMED IN ONE FISCAL YEAR, and where it was read from. The pool is the noun ABC allocates: costs are gathered into it by activity first and only then pushed out to blocks, which is the whole difference between activity-based costing and dividing the overhead account by the acreage. `sources` is not decoration — it is the itemised trail from the pool figure back to the cost centers and accounts that produced it, so a pool is never a number somebody asserts. A pool keyed in by hand is allowed and is labelled Manual, because the alternative is an operation that cannot cost an activity until its chart of accounts is perfect.

fields.description: The year this pool belongs to. Part of the identity: one activity has one pool per year, and two pools for one activity and year would make 'what did spraying cost' depend on which row was read first.
fields.label: Fiscal Year

fields.description: The window the ledger was read over. Defaulted from the Fiscal Year and stored on the row rather than re-derived, because a fiscal year's dates can be edited afterwards and a pool that silently re-scoped itself would change a prior year's allocation with nothing on the record saying so.
fields.label: Period Start

fields.description: What this activity cost over the period, before any of it is pushed out to a block.
fields.label: Pool Amount

fields.description: LEDGER means the figure was totalled off GL Entry over the activity's cost center and accounts, and `sources` itemises it. MANUAL means somebody typed it. The distinction is on the record because a manual pool is a perfectly legitimate figure and an entirely different kind of evidence, and a report that presented the two identically would be claiming a traceability half its rows do not have.
fields.label: Amount Source

fields.description: Draft is excluded from allocation; Ready is included; Allocated is set by `compute_abc_allocation` once a run has consumed it. Allocated pools are still re-read by later runs — the flag records that a run has happened, it does not lock the pool, because a corrected pool that could not be re-allocated would freeze an error in place.
fields.label: Status

fields.description: The one block this pool goes to in full. Meaningful ONLY where the activity's driver is Direct Assignment — a cost that was incurred for one block and no other, which is the honest way to model replant on a single field rather than inventing a driver to spread it.
fields.label: Cost Object (Field)

fields.description: One row per cost center or account that contributed, with what it contributed and how many ledger entries stand behind it. The trail from the pool back to the books.
fields.label: Sources

name: Activity Cost Pool
